source.title: Australia passes the Digital Duty of Care Act, an online safety law that exposes Big Tech to multibillion-dollar fines for failing to prevent foreseeable harms (Rod McGuirk/Associated Press)
source.text: Rod McGuirk / Associated Press : Australia passes the Digital Duty of Care Act, an online safety law that exposes Big Tech to multibillion-dollar fines for failing to prevent foreseeable harms — Australia's Parliament on Wednesday passed online safety laws that could expose tech giants to multibillion-dollar fines for failing to prevent foreseeable online harms.

draft.headline: Australia passes the Digital Duty of Care Act, exposing Big Tech to multibillion-dollar fines for failing to prevent foreseeable online harms.
draft.threads_post:
Australia just passed the Digital Duty of Care Act.

Parliament passed the online safety law on Wednesday. It targets tech giants operating in the country. Under the new rules, companies face multibillion-dollar fines if they fail to prevent foreseeable online harms.

Will multibillion-dollar fines force Big Tech to change, or will they just pay up?
